title: Crash
events_chronological: Persian shopkeeper Farhad and his daughter Dorri buy a handgun while the dealer mocks his English.
Anthony and Peter carjack district attorney Rick Cabot's SUV outside a restaurant.
Officer Ryan pulls over the Thayers, gropes Christine in front of her husband Cameron, and lets them go with a warning.
Ryan's partner Hansen asks their commander for a new patrol car rather than keep riding with a racist.
Locksmith Daniel changes the Cabots' locks while Jean loudly assumes he is a gang member about to sell her keys.
Daniel replaces the lock on Farhad's shop and warns him the door itself is broken, and Farhad accuses him of running a con.
Ryan pleads with HMO clerk Shaniqua Johnson for treatment for his father and is refused.
Farhad's shop is smashed and looted overnight, and the insurer refuses to pay because he ignored the warning about the door.
Christine is trapped upside down in a burning wreck and Ryan, the officer who assaulted her, crawls in and drags her out.
Anthony and Peter run down a Korean man, Choi, and dump him outside a hospital.
Cameron is stopped mid-carjacking of his own car and Hansen talks the other officers out of shooting him.
Cameron drives Anthony away from the police at speed and then throws him out of the car.
Farhad waits outside Daniel's house with the gun and fires just as Daniel's small daughter Lara runs into his arms.
The child is untouched - Dorri had bought blanks - and Farhad decides she is his angel.
Hansen picks up Peter hitchhiking, misreads him reaching into his pocket, shoots him dead and burns the car.
Detective Graham Waters is called to a body dumped by the roadside and finds that it is his brother Peter.
Graham's mother blames him for never once going to look for his brother.
Jean falls down her stairs and tells her housekeeper Maria that she is the only friend she has.
Anthony finds Choi's van packed with trafficked Cambodians and turns them loose in Chinatown instead of selling them.
In the first snow over Los Angeles another collision starts another argument in the street.
syuzhet_notes: The film opens on told-order bullet 1, a scene from near the end of the story, then a title card reads "Yesterday" and the rest runs as a largely forward-moving braid of intercut strands. The opening moment recurs in the last act at the point where the film catches up with it, so the discovery of the body is both the first and the sixteenth thing the audience sees.
fabula_notes: The strands overlap rather than following one another and the film offers almost no time markers, so the ordering within a given day is inferred from causal links - Farhad's shop is looted after Daniel's warning, Christine's rescue follows Ryan's traffic stop. That the body in the opening scene is Graham's brother is withheld and only becomes legible in retrospect.
